rubrics.criterion: After the refactor, the contract (or set of contracts) behind the state-session flow is one that every backend the config factory can return implements meaningfully: each state-persistence member reachable through the runtime context singleton (restore, save, and the stale-session sweep) is genuinely exercised when that backend is selected, and no member of that contract is a placeholder-only obligation for any selectable backend.
rubrics.rationale: This is the core interface-segregation outcome for the state-session side of this task: the fat shared session-store contract forced every backend to carry members whose dispatchers exist only for other stores. A solver can satisfy this with differently-shaped cohesive contracts; the graded fact is that backends no longer declare obligations for capabilities their flow cannot reach.

rubrics.criterion: The pending-cookie redemption store ends up answerable only for redemption-style behavior: the state-session persistence, stale-session sweep, state encoding/decoding, and state-token minting obligations it previously carried are no longer declared on, inherited by, or required of the cookie store, because its only reachable dispatchers are the render-time enqueue and the /__apply-cookies redemption.
rubrics.rationale: The cookie cache was the most structurally distant store dragged onto the shared session-store contract in this instance; removing its unrelated obligations is the second half of the smell's resolution and cannot be substituted by keeping refusals that merely raise.

rubrics.criterion: Token minting for state events lives where it is actually exercised: the event-creation code path mints a state token through whatever home the refactor chose, and no concrete store is left required to provide a minting (or hand-rolled admission) member that no reachable call path can invoke on it.
rubrics.rationale: Minting and admission were spread onto all stores by the wide contract in this case (only one backend ever uses the admission predicate; minting had exactly one production caller). The graded fact is the location of these responsibilities after the change, not their names.

rubrics.criterion: No concrete store in this layer still carries a capability obligation that no production call site can dispatch on that store: after the fix there is no store class for which an interface-mandated member exists solely to satisfy a wide contract (e.g. a state backend still required to provide cookie redemption, or any store required to provide a codec/admission/minting member nothing can invoke on it).
rubrics.rationale: This is the negative restatement of the instance's smell relation: it fires when a solution only partially splits the contract or renames the obligations while keeping them attached to stores that cannot use them.

rubrics.criterion: No placeholder-style member survives anywhere in this store layer: no method whose body is only a not-implemented marker, a pass, or an unconditional refuse-to-run raise remains on any concrete store or shared base in the refactored layer.
rubrics.rationale: Stub-deletion pressure is the defining cleanup half of interface segregation for this codebase; leaving inert members behind (even with cleaned-up inheritance) means the dependency boundary was not actually narrowed.

rubrics.criterion: Every call-site consumer of the state-session flow was kept consistent with the refactored contracts: the runtime context's restore and save operations plus the WSGI teardown sweep still dispatch successfully against every backend the config factory can select, and the state-token minting site in the event-creation path works against whatever backend configuration selects.
rubrics.rationale: In this instance the consumers live outside the touched store modules (runtime context, teardown, event creation); a split that only edits store classes but leaves any consumer pointed at a capability some selectable backend no longer provides is incomplete.

rubrics.criterion: The cookie flow's call sites were updated coherently with the cookie store's final shape: the render-time pending-cookie enqueue and the /__apply-cookies redemption both operate against the post-refactor cookie store (or its replacement) with matching names, so enqueue-then-redeem still works end to end.
rubrics.rationale: The redemption store is module-private with two known dispatchers; refactors of its contract that forget either call site are a plausible failure mode specific to this instance.

rubrics.criterion: The cookie redemption store no longer references state-session persistence or dataclass-codec declarations in any form: no inheritance edge, implemented-interface obligation, import, or annotation tying it to state persistence or state serialization remains in its module.
rubrics.rationale: The coupling can survive a nominal split under a different spelling (e.g. keeping the cookie store a subtype of something that still carries state-persistence members); this catches residual dependence rather than surface-level separation.

rubrics.criterion: The dataclass encode/decode logic and the token minting logic that were displaced by the refactor ended up in a home that production code actually uses: every declaration of these responsibilities left in the tree is imported/called by production backend or consumer code (or was deleted), with no second, orphaned copy kept beside the live one.
rubrics.rationale: This instance removed module-level codec and token helpers and moved them behind the interface; a repair that re-homes them for real stores must not leave the old declarations or duplicate dead copies behind.

rubrics.criterion: Whatever interface/template modules this layer ends with are all load-bearing: any module holding contract or template-base declarations for this store layer is imported and used by production code after the change, or has been deleted (with re-exports for the test-visible import surface kept where the existing tests need them, e.g. the States type and the backend names from their current module).
rubrics.rationale: The instance introduced a dedicated interface module for the wide contract; a sound repair may split or delete it, but an orphaned declaration-only module (or a broken test import surface) is a concrete failure mode of this task.

rubrics.criterion: No dead references to the former wide contract linger: touched production files contain no import of a contract/template name they no longer use, no now-unused exception or typing import, and no alias that exists only to keep the old shape compiling.
rubrics.rationale: Leftover imports are the specific residue this instance's design invites (several modules imported the shared contract name), and their presence indicates a mechanical rather than semantic repair.

rubrics.criterion: Per-backend state semantics are preserved: token lookup on restore (including the exact miss diagnostics), the one-restore-per-token consumption behavior, per-backend save formats, the TTL sweep behavior of each backend, the SQL backend's request-count gating, and the disabled-sessions no-op/refusal behavior all behave exactly as before the change.
rubrics.rationale: These behaviors are the payload of the state-session machinery in this repository; the refactor was requested as behavior-invisible and these are the concrete per-backend invariants a partial or careless split would break.

rubrics.criterion: The file-backed state store still applies its token-conformance guard before deriving or touching any filesystem path from a state token, so path-traversal through a crafted token is still rejected in the same way.
rubrics.rationale: The admission predicate is the one inherited member that has a genuine per-store user in this instance; refactors that delete it wholesale or apply it after path derivation would silently drop existing filesystem protection.

rubrics.criterion: Pending-cookie redemption remains one-time and time-boxed: an enqueued cookie batch can be redeemed exactly once with a valid signed token, replay or unknown-token submissions still fail as before, and an expired token is still rejected rather than applied.
rubrics.rationale: The cookie flow is the second consumer whose behavior the prompt bounds; windowing and one-time redemption are the security-meaningful invariants of this machinery in this repository.

rubrics.criterion: State tokens are emitted to clients exactly when state sessions are enabled (and never otherwise), and a minted token still has the same randomness characteristics as before the change, whatever module now owns minting.
rubrics.rationale: The minting site is a public protocol behavior of the SSE event payload in this instance; a refactor that starts minting for disabled deployments, stops minting, or switches the token generator to a weaker form would change observable wire behavior.
